$comment: Floors for the tb2-cross-section suite (bench/suites/tb2-cross-section.txt).
A run below a floor fails the gate. A floor that cannot be measured on the
run leaves the gate unverifiable, which exits 2 and is not a pass.
No maxCostPerAcceptedOutcomeUsd. The lane this suite runs on serves
gpt-5.6-luna, which the forge model catalog deliberately leaves unpriced,
so cost per accepted outcome resolves to unknown on every proxy run, and a
dollar ceiling declared here would be unverifiable on every healthy run -
the gate would exit 2 forever, which is a gate nobody reads (#125). The
same reasoning is recorded on tb2-quick.json, whose comment assumed the
proxy lane was priced; it is not, for the one model these suites use.
When the catalog prices gpt-5.6-luna with accepted rates, restore the
ceiling in the same change that makes the measurement real, so the floor
and its measurability land together.
acceptPlaceholderRates is deliberately absent: every rate in the forge
model catalog is marked provisional today, so a dollar ceiling scored
against them would be scored against a guess. Set it to true only for a
relative regression check, and say so when you do.
minSuccessRate starts low on purpose. It is a floor that catches a
regression, not a target that flatters a number, and it should be raised
as scheduled runs establish what the lane actually holds.
